hyperedges.label: Calendar interchange with retained Journal storage

nodes.label: Kalender in der Seitenleiste
nodes.rationale: Year, month, week, workweek and day views follow the journal date. The sidebar width is at least 280 pixels and leaves at least 420 pixels for the journal.

nodes.label: Nur im Kalender entry choice
nodes.rationale: Calendar-only is a peer choice beside event and task. These entries remain editable, stored and exportable but do not appear in the daily note. Changing the choice back to event or task restores daily-note visibility.

nodes.label: Calendar UID identity
nodes.rationale: Matching calendar UIDs update existing occurrences rather than creating duplicate entries.

nodes.label: CodeMirror-6
nodes.rationale: Each entry uses a live-preview editor. Formatting markers are visible only around the cursor or selection, while storage retains complete Markdown text. Code, links and formulas are intentionally unsupported.

nodes.label: Eingebettet
nodes.rationale: The inline action layout displays actions as words within the text flow without a separate window, background or shadow.

nodes.label: journal:changed event
nodes.rationale: The calendar learns which days were saved through the journal:changed Tauri event.

nodes.label: localStorage
nodes.rationale: Action layout and sidebar width are device-local preferences rather than journal database content.

nodes.label: Mini-Kalender date picker
nodes.rationale: Clicking the date or pressing Ctrl+G opens the application's compact calendar instead of the native Windows date picker.

nodes.label: @fontsource
nodes.rationale: Lilex and IBM Plex Sans are bundled through @fontsource under OFL-1.1 and work offline without separately installed fonts.

nodes.label: Satelliten
nodes.rationale: The orbit action layout places round animated action satellites around the entry symbol while keeping the text unobstructed.

nodes.label: src-tauri/src/storage.rs persistence
nodes.rationale: The storage module manages validation, database migrations and SQLite transactions.

nodes.label: Wischen
nodes.rationale: The swipe action layout maps directional gestures on an entry symbol to planning, deletion, status and priority actions; the chosen layout is stored locally.

nodes.label: npm.cmd test
nodes.rationale: npm.cmd test covers entry grouping, priority ordering, reordering, planning, calendars, clock input and Markdown behavior.

nodes.label: Rust-Tests
nodes.rationale: Rust database tests cover persistence, validation, migrations, stale writes, entry status, linked planning and reopening database files. The README test count is historical, not a current measured result.

nodes.label: check:ui
nodes.rationale: The Edge UI check uses official Tauri IPC mocks and synthetic in-memory data without opening the real SQLite database. It does not replace manual native-window or installer tests.

nodes.label: Atomic SQLite day transaction
nodes.rationale: Saving replaces the entries of one day inside a SQLite transaction, creates previously absent planning targets and updates the revisions of affected days.

nodes.label: Atomic calendar import
nodes.rationale: Import runs as one transaction, shows a preview and preserves unrelated entries and daily contents.

nodes.label: Debounced autosave at 0.7 seconds
nodes.rationale: Daily notes save after a 0.7-second typing pause; Ctrl+S saves immediately. Pending changes are saved before navigation or closing. Failed saves prevent navigation or request explicit confirmation before closing.

nodes.label: Calendar timezone interpretation
nodes.rationale: Import supports all-day and timed events, dated tasks, UTC, local time, IANA timezones and embedded timezone definitions.

nodes.label: Calendar export boundary
nodes.rationale: Export includes tasks and events from every day, including calendar-only entries. It excludes free text, daily titles, notes and planning traces. Tasks are represented as events with additional Journal type information.

nodes.label: Calendar import conversion limits
nodes.rationale: Recurring events are expanded from the previous year through the end of the second following year. Multi-day events become daily entries. Export does not reconstruct recurrence rules. Imports are limited to 5 MB and 5000 entries, do not delete removed occurrences automatically, and do not move entries already planned onward.

nodes.label: Local calendar dates
nodes.rationale: Days are identified by local calendar date rather than UTC timestamps; new entries receive UUIDs.

nodes.label: Reminders without notifications
nodes.rationale: The reminder preference is stored and displayed as a bell, but notifications are not implemented.

nodes.label: Linked multi-day planning
nodes.rationale: Planning to other dates creates target entries once and leaves a trace. Text, kind and priority propagate through linked groups; status and time remain occurrence-specific. Group actions can target this occurrence, following occurrences or all linked entries.

nodes.label: Revision prevents stale writes
nodes.rationale: A revision prevents an older day snapshot from overwriting newer stored content. This does not constitute a synchronization conflict strategy.

nodes.label: Synchronization not implemented
nodes.rationale: ICS import is not synchronization. Full journal backups and automatic synchronization are not implemented; synchronization would need explicit deletion, version and conflict modeling.

nodes.label: Calendar task status rendering
nodes.rationale: Completed tasks are greyed out. Cancelled tasks are greyed out and struck through; completion alone does not add strikethrough.

nodes.label: Touched-day cache invalidation
nodes.rationale: Save responses report affected days in touched so the frontend can discard cached states after linked planning changes.

nodes.label: Unified toolbar and titlebar
nodes.rationale: Daily navigation and date sit beside minimize, maximize/restore and close controls in one application toolbar; blank areas drag the window and double-click toggles maximization.
